clue.text: Improvised speech, sadly mostly ribald

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters left are put into a new order
mostly means not quite all of the word ribald is used: one letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone's off-the-cuff remarks were, regrettably, largely smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the R of RIBALD, leaving IBALD, and 'sadly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An unscripted remark made up on the spot is an ad lib, from the Latin for 'at pleasure'.

clue.text: Becoming a despot in Australasia

indicators.note: becoming signals a change of form, so the letters that follow turn into something else

explanation.surface: Someone turns into a tyrant while living in Australia or New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' rearranges the nine letters of A DESPOT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Britons have long called Australia and New Zealand the Antipodes, the lands on the far side of the globe.

clue.text: Camp marching order about seniority

indicators.note: about means going round, so the order's letters sit either side of the other piece

parts.note: left, right is the marching order, abbreviated to L and R
seniority is a matter of age

explanation.surface: In a military camp, a drill command is given concerning rank by length of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marching order' is the drill-sergeant's 'left, right', L R; 'about' puts it round AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager or lager is a defensive camp, especially one ringed by wagons, from Afrikaans and German.

clue.text: Mannish queen is a murderer

parts.note: butch describes a masculine manner or look
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A masculine-looking queen turns out to be a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brutal killer who slaughters people is called a butcher.

clue.text: Excited clapper at Shavian play

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic member of the audience applauds at a George Bernard Shaw play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' rearranges CLAPPER AT. Shavian means by George Bernard Shaw, who wrote The Apple Cart (1929).
explanation.definitionFit: The Apple Cart is a political comedy by George Bernard Shaw, the adjective Shavian referring to him.

clue.text: A little oregano in the salad oil

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pinch of a herb goes in the salad, which is then dressed with oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'salad oil' as the definition, but ANOINT means to oil, not salad oil; 'salad' only belongs to the phrase the run is hidden in, oreg-ANO IN T-he.
explanation.definitionFit: To anoint is to rub or smear with oil, as in a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Making toast is an undertaking

definitions.meaning: raising one's glass to drink someone's health
the act of giving a solemn promise

explanation.definitionFit: To pledge someone is an old phrase for drinking their health, and a pledge is also a binding promise.

clue.text: Empress with English upper-class servant who appears by magic

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage
a genie is the spirit summoned from a lamp to serve its owner

explanation.surface: An empress keeps a well-bred English attendant who materialises by sorcery.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from 1950s British talk of 'U and non-U' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugénie was the wife of Napoleon III and the last Empress of the French.

clue.text: It's opening the door to advertising on religious activities

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: AD is short for an advertisement
a mission is the work of spreading a faith

explanation.surface: Advertising is what gets you a hearing with church evangelists.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is entry, letting someone in through the door.

clue.text: Devon resort that shall be nameless — it's got gambling machines!

indicators.note: a place that shall be nameless loses its name, so the letter for name is removed

parts.note: Totnes is a town in Devon, in south-west England

explanation.surface: A Devon holiday town too embarrassing to name turns out to be full of slot machines.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name; take it from TOTNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tote is short for totalisator, the betting machine that pools stakes, so the plural names several of them.

clue.text: Take a firm line here and tread carefully

definitions.text: Take a firm line here and tread carefully

parts.words: Take a firm line here and tread carefully
parts.note: the firm line is a taut rope literally walked by a circus performer, who must step with great care

explanation.surface: Advice to be resolute yet cautious in a delicate situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A taut wire or rope high up is where an acrobat walks, placing each step precisely.

clue.text: Miss Hepburn ran it from A to B emotionally, said Miss Parker

definitions.text: Miss Hepburn ran it from A to B emotionally, said Miss Parker

parts.words: Miss Hepburn ran it from A to B emotionally, said Miss Parker
parts.note: Dorothy Parker's famous jibe at Katharine Hepburn was that her performance ran the whole range of emotions only from A to B

explanation.surface: A recollection of a famous theatre critic's put-down of an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is the full range of something, as in running through every emotion.

clue.text: Maiden production of The Ensign's Opera

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of material, so the words are reworked into fresh order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and both S letters are used

explanation.surface: The first night of a comic opera titled after a junior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' rearranges the fifteen letters of THE ENSIGNS OPERA, counting the possessive S.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Greek parthenos, virgin, it is reproduction without a male, a maidenly birth.

clue.text: Go ashore and silence the dog?

definitions.meaning: to leave a ship and land
read as ..., to stop a dog from barking

explanation.definitionFit: To debark is to disembark, and humorously it is also removing a dog's bark.

clue.text: Steady principal in musical comedy

definitions.meaning: Sandy Wilson's 1950s musical comedy, its title role being the lead

explanation.definitionFit: A girl's steady is her regular sweetheart, and Sandy Wilson's musical comedy is titled after one.

clue.text: Curling one's lip, like Pooh-Bah at birth

definitions.meaning: Pooh-Bah, the haughty official in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, claims he was born that way

explanation.definitionFit: A curled lip is a contemptuous expression, and Pooh-Bah boasts in The Mikado that he was born with it.

clue.text: Friend starting to turn green in the main

indicators.note: starting places the rearranged colour at the beginning, before the companion
to turn means to change round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A companion begins to feel sick with envy or nausea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' makes the colour an anagram, and 'starting' puts that anagram at the front, ahead of the word for friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main and generally are both idioms for usually, as a rule.

clue.text: The stance for the approach

definitions.meaning: a posture or position of the body
one's way of thinking about or handling something

explanation.definitionFit: Attitude names both a bodily posture and a mental outlook or manner.

clue.text: Cunning fellow making surreptitious profits

parts.note: sly means furtive or secret
boot is an old word for profit or advantage, as in 'to boot'

explanation.surface: A crafty man makes money on the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A slyboots is an informal term for a crafty, artful person.

clue.text: Rebel as Roman galley slave

indicators.note: to rebel is to rise up and overturn order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Roman rower chained to his bench rises in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Galley slaves were made to row, so each was a rower at the oar.

clue.text: Piece about new number and name

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A newspaper article concerning a fresh figure and title.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is an artillery gun, and a cannon is one.

clue.text: Article is in demand — it is full of flavour

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in places the small word inside the word for demand

parts.note: need means a demand or requirement

explanation.surface: A grammar point is sought after, and it proves very tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'it is full of flavour' read like a comment, but it is the definition; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is the seed of anise, used as a strongly aromatic, liquorice-like flavouring.

clue.text: Light studies for quantity surveyors in the licensing trade

definitions.meaning: the science of how light behaves

definitions.text: quantity surveyors in the licensing trade
definitions.meaning: in pubs, the devices fixed to upturned spirit bottles that measure out a shot

explanation.definitionFit: Optics is the branch of physics dealing with light, and in British pubs an optic is a measured-dose spirit dispenser.

clue.text: One whose clients are likely to be framed and go to the wall

definitions.text: One whose clients are likely to be framed and go to the wall

parts.words: One whose clients are likely to be framed and go to the wall
parts.note: sounds like a crooked lawyer whose clients are stitched up and ruined, but the clients' likenesses are put in frames and hung

explanation.surface: A hapless lawyer whose customers end up wrongly convicted and bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who paints likenesses has sitters whose pictures are framed and hung on walls.

clue.text: Adhesive is spread round top of stamp

indicators.note: round means going about, so the spread's letters surround the single letter

parts.note: pâté is a savoury spread

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the word stamp

explanation.surface: Glue is smeared around the upper edge of a postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' gives S from 'stamp'; 'round' puts PATE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a soft glue, as used for wallpaper.

clue.text: The ending of want demands job

definitions.note: the definition is singular while the answer is a plural noun

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, here from want

parts.note: asks means demands or requests

explanation.surface: Being out of work ends when someone finally insists on employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ending of' takes T from 'want'. The singular 'job' defines a plural answer, a looseness of the setter's.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, the same as a job.

clue.text: Cook showing energy

definitions.meaning: to cook with vapour from boiling water
power or drive, as in running out of puff

explanation.definitionFit: Steam is a cooking method using vapour, and the word also means vigour, as in 'full steam ahead'.

clue.text: Kind of joint common to all mankind

definitions.meaning: a mechanical coupling that lets shafts turn at an angle

explanation.definitionFit: A universal joint couples two angled shafts, and the adjective also means applying to everyone.

clue.text: Destroy nettles in hazards

parts.note: to end something is to destroy it
to nettle someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: Wiping out stinging plants among risky obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to put it at risk, which is to imperil it.

clue.text: Dark river, extremely dirty to go across

indicators.note: the outer letters straddle the river's name, going across it on both sides
extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters of dirty

parts.note: the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: A murky river, so filthy that no one would cross it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives D and Y from 'dirty', which 'to go across' places either side of USK, a Welsh river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusky means dim or shadowy, darkish in colour.
